Q: How can I loop through a JSON file using bash and extract values to variables? A:

1. Use jq only once!!

Try this:

while IFS=, read -r envName val1 val2; do
    echo "for $envName the first value is $val1 and the second value is $val2"
done < <(
    jq -r '.[] | to_entries[] | .key + "," + ( .value | join(",") )' < vars.json
)

for environment1 the first value is Value1 and the second value is Value2
for environment2 the first value is Value3 and the second value is Value4

1.1. With undefined length of array

or this:

while IFS=, read -ra row; do
    envName="${row[0]}" vals=("${row[@]:1}")
    echo "for $envName values are: [ ${vals[*]@Q} ]"
done < <(
   jq -r '.[] | to_entries[] | .key + "," + ( .value | join(",") )' < vars.json
)

for environment1 values are: [ 'Value1' 'Value2' ]
for environment2 values are: [ 'Value3' 'Value4' ]

1.2. Using alternative separator

If some comma could be found in some of your contents, you may use any other ASCII separator.

For sample using BELL character 0x07 ( see man ASCII):

   005   5     05    ENQ (enquiry)             
   006   6     06    ACK (acknowledge)         
   007   7     07    BEL '\a' (bell)           
   010   8     08    BS  '\b' (backspace)      
   011   9     09    HT  '\t' (horizontal tab) 
   012   10    0A    LF  '\n' (new line)       

while IFS=$'\a' read -ra row; do
    envName="${row[0]}" vals=("${row[@]:1}")
    printf 'For \e[3m%s\e[0m, values are: [ \e[3m%s\e[0m ]\n' \
        "$envName" "${vals[*]@Q}"
done < <(
    jq -r '.[] | to_entries[] |
        "\( .key )\u0007\( .value | join("\u0007") )"' < vars.json
)

For environment1, values are: [ 'Value1' 'Value2' ]
For environment2, values are: [ 'Value3' 'Value4' ]

Notice:

  • the use of printf instead of echo
  • Syntax: \( .key )\u0007\( .value | join("\u0007") ) instead of .key + "," + ( .value | join(",") ) for same result.

2. But if you really wanna do bash loops

For sample, but whenever possible, avoid doing repetitive fork to same utility for asking same static file.

Regarding @pmf comment, I use keys_unsorted instead of keys in order to prevent automatic sort by jq.

while read -r envName; do
    { read -r val1;
      read -r val2 ; } < <(
          jq -r ".[].$envName|.[]" vars.json
    )
    echo "for $envName the first value is $val1 and the second value is $val2"
done < <(
    jq -r '.[] | keys_unsorted | .[]' <vars.json
)

for environment1 the first value is Value1 and the second value is Value2
for environment2 the first value is Value3 and the second value is Value4

2.1. With undefined length of array

while read -r envName; do
    mapfile -t vals < <(
        jq -r ".[].$envName | .[]" vars.json
    )
    echo "for $envName, values are: [ ${vals[*]@Q} ]"
done < <(
    jq -r '.[] | keys_unsorted | .[]' <vars.json
)

for environment1, values are: [ 'Value1' 'Value2' ]
for environment2, values are: [ 'Value3' 'Value4' ]

2.3 One fork by variable

But if you really want to populate each variable for himself, you could:

while read -r envName; do
    val1="$( jq -r ".[].$envName.variable1" vars.json )"
    val2="$( jq -r ".[].$envName.variable2" vars.json )"
    echo "for $envName the first value is $val1 and the second value is $val2"
done < <(
    jq -r '.[] | keys_unsorted | .[]' < vars.json
)

for environment1 the first value is Value1 and the second value is Value2
for environment2 the first value is Value3 and the second value is Value4

Q: codeigniter active records group_by returns random ordering of joined table record id A:

I recommend building the subquery as a precompile string, then injecting that safely built subquery into the select() call of the parent query build.

public function shopItems(int $userId, ?int $limit = null, ?int $start = null): array
{
    date_default_timezone_set('Asia/Colombo');
    $expire = date('Y-m-d');

    $sub = $this->db
        ->select('image')
        ->where('item_id = items.id')
        ->order_by('gallery_id')
        ->limit(1)
        ->get_compiled_select('item_gallery');

    return $this->db
        ->select("*, ($sub) profile_img")
        ->join('item_gallery', 'items.id = item_gallery.item_id', 'left')
        ->where_in('items.status', ['yes', 'edit'])
        ->where(['items.exp_date >' => $expire, 'items.user_id' => $userId])
        ->group_by('item_gallery.item_id')
        ->order_by('items.post_date', 'desc')
        ->get('items', $limit, $start)
        ->result();
}

Assuming values like $userId = 1, $limit = 10, and $start = 0, the SQL will be rendered similar to (I improve the spacing for readability):

SELECT *,
    (
       SELECT `image`
       FROM `item_gallery`
       WHERE `item_id` = `items`.`id`
       ORDER BY `gallery_id`
       LIMIT 1
    ) profile_img
FROM `items`
LEFT JOIN `item_gallery` ON `items`.`id` = `item_gallery`.`item_id`
WHERE `items`.`status` IN('yes', 'edit')
    AND `items`.`exp_date` > '2026-01-09'
    AND `items`.`user_id` = 1
GROUP BY `item_gallery`.`item_id`
ORDER BY `items`.`post_date` DESC
LIMIT 10

Q: After upgrade, Flyway initialization fails with "Unknown prefix for location" A:

Issue resolved by switching the order of the Gradle dependencies:

implementation(libs.flyway.postgresql)
implementation(libs.flyway.core)

The root cause - that ShadowJar's task mergeServiceFiles() isn't properly merging Java Service Provider Interface (SPI) files from multiple Flyway jars. Flyway uses Java's ServiceLoader to discover location handlers via META-INF/services/org.flywaydb.core.extensibility.Plugin, and in my case, because my PostgreSQL plugin was listed after Flyway core, it overwritten the plugins available by Flyway core - including the plugin for fetching a classloader resource. The giveaway was the empty list of available plugins in the error message - the part where it said should be one of had an empty list. The reason I saw the callback path is that this is an automatic step during initialization that's generally fails silently if it's not there.

Q: How andle daylight saving time in multi stack app A:

The only way I found was deal the time as UTC.

UTC time is not effected by dayligth saving time, in this way I have not ordering problem.

So the first step was setting Laravel time zone as UTC:

config>app.php:

'timezone' => 'UTC',

This was a good way, but if you need to operate with Carbon::now() you have to remind that now will be served in server time zone, so you will need to "UTC" the now datetime!

Carbon::now('UTC')

Using UTC as base time, introduce another "problem", but problems has solutions:

Doing daily report I cannot directly use Carbon startofDay() end endofDay() functions, but I need to create one date with my local time zone, get the start and the end of the day and then convert each to UTC time zone:

        $day = new Carbon($SingleDay);
        $day->setTimezone('Europe/Rome');
        $startTime = $day->copy()->startOfDay();
        $endTime = $day->copy()->endOfDay();
        $startTime->setTimezone('UTC');
        $endTime->setTimezone('UTC');

And the phyton script also is changed, returning the UTCnow datetime for storing data:

datetime.utcnow()

For recovering data from the database, I wrote a query removing one hour or two depending from the day, a short work that helped me to recovery all data
